document_type: Rotary vs Piston Engine Technical Analysis
purpose: Comprehensive comparison of Wankel rotary and reciprocating piston engines

piston_engine.conversion: Connecting rod converts linear to rotational via crankshaft

rotary_engine.valvetrain: NONE - ports exposed by rotor position
rotary_engine.power_cycles: Same 4-stroke cycle, but 3 chambers operating simultaneously

comparison.ratio: Rotary produces 2.3x more power per liter

power_density.reason: Three power pulses per rotor revolution vs one per two revolutions (4-cyl)

comparison.ratio: Rotary is 45% lighter for equivalent power

weight.reason: Far fewer parts, no reciprocating mass, compact design

comparison.note: Rotary fits in spaces piston engines cannot

physical_size.reason: No reciprocating motion requires no tall deck height

details.vibration_source_piston: Pistons reversing direction creates primary/secondary imbalance
details.vibration_source_rotary: Only eccentric mass - minimal and easily balanced
details.result: Rotary idles smoother than most piston engines

smoothness.reason: No reciprocating mass means no reciprocating vibration

comparison.note: Rotary achieves this with no valve float concerns

high_rpm_capability.reason: No valves to float, no pistons decelerating at TDC/BDC

parts_count.reason: No camshaft, valves, lifters, timing components

fuel_economy.reason: Long combustion chamber, high surface-to-volume ratio, apex seal leakage

issues: Apex seal gaps allow unburned fuel passage
emissions.reason: Combustion chamber geometry and sealing inherently produce more HCs

thermal_efficiency.reason: Heat loss through larger chamber surface area

low_speed_torque.characteristic: Rotary power band favors high RPM

rotary_specific: Oil consumption is normal (must top up)
Apex seal replacement is eventual necessity
piston_specific: More components that can fail individually

rotary_excels: Applications where character matters over efficiency

engineering_compromises.summary: Rotary trades efficiency for power density and character

rotaries_always_burn_oil.reality: Yes - by design. This lubricates apex seals. It's not a defect.

rotaries_cant_make_torque.reality: Turbo rotaries make excellent torque - just at higher RPM

rotaries_are_outdated.context: Rotary advantages still relevant in specific applications

the_ultimate_question.question: Why would anyone choose a rotary over a piston engine?
the_ultimate_question.answer: Because some things cannot be measured on a spreadsheet
factors_beyond_specs: The connection to a unique engineering legacy
The membership in a passionate community
The satisfaction of understanding something others don't
